reading.body:
CyrusOne Norwalk (NYM5) holds 4 MW of published IT capacity across 168,000 square feet in Norwalk, Connecticut. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this is roughly 100 racks. The facility's total MW is not published, so the IT load represents only a disclosed portion of the campus.

Norwalk ranks first among Connecticut's five mapped data center facilities by published capacity and accounts for half of the state's 8 MW of published IT load. Connecticut's two facilities with published specifications suggest limited transparency across the state's data center footprint. The campus carries SSAE 16 Type II certification, which qualifies it to host systems requiring audited security and availability controls.

The CyrusOne Norwalk campus is part of a tri-state cluster spanning Connecticut and the Hudson Valley. CyrusOne was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. Without published total capacity, the campus's relevance to AI scaling depends on how much undisclosed capacity lies behind the 4 MW figure and whether this private acquisition signals deployment plans in the region.
